diagram_math_checks.checks: A_n has alpha_i=e_i-e_(i+1): squared norms 2, inner product -1 exactly between consecutive indices. B_n keeps consecutive differences then e_n, giving norms 2,...,2,1 and final Cartan pair (-1,-2), hence two edges with arrow n-1 to n. C_n ends 2e_n, giving norms 2,...,2,4, final inner product -2 and Cartan pair (-2,-1), hence arrow n to n-1. D_n ends e_(n-1)-e_n and e_(n-1)+e_n; these are orthogonal, both pair -1 with alpha_(n-2), and all norms are 2. The general recipes cover A1 (no edge), B2,C3,D4 without repeated vertices. Actual representative counts: A4 4 vertices/3 strokes, B4 and C4 4/4, D5 5/4; D5 degrees 1,2,3,1,1.

diagram_math_checks.checks: All four vectors belong to the 48-root set. Exact rational enumeration verifies rank 4 and integral coordinates of one sign for every root, confirming the proposed base. Squared norms are [2,2,1,1]; only nonzero off-diagonal products are (1,2)=-1,(2,3)=-1,(3,4)=-1/2. Thus edges 1-2 and 3-4 are single, 2-3 double with arrow 2 to 3. Native picture contains 4 vertices and 4 edge strokes.

diagram_math_checks.checks: The half-root alpha1 has six minus signs, belongs to Phi8 and satisfies x7+x8=x6+x8=0. Alpha2 and alpha3 through alpha6 use first five coordinates; adding alpha7 spans V7 and adding alpha8 spans R8. Exact rational enumeration of the actual restricted root sets gives 72,126,240 roots, ranks 6,7,8, and integral coordinates of one sign for every root in the respective proposed bases. All squared norms equal 2. Nonzero off-diagonal products are -1 on (1,3),(3,4),(2,4),(4,5),(5,6), then (6,7) and (7,8) as rank permits, and zero elsewhere. Thus the single-edge trees have 6/5,7/6,8/7 vertices/edges, branch vertex 4 of degree 3, and arms (2,1,2),(2,1,3),(2,1,4), respectively. Native picture visually matches these exact trees.

Squared norms 6 and 2, inner product -3: a12=2*(-3)/6=-1 and a21=2*(-3)/2=-3, matching the displayed matrix under the local denominator-row convention. Product 3 gives three edges, and the shorter beta is vertex 2, so the arrow points 1 to 2. Native image has 2 vertices, 3 parallel strokes and the right-pointing chevron.

No morphisms, crossings or commutative squares are asserted. Every depicted relation is adjacency, multiplicity or long-to-short orientation under the local Dynkin definition. The original rigorous proof remains byte-identical and independent of the figure; no proof step cites the atlas.
